newsitem.title: UK: Britain jails Palestinians for Israeli embassy bomb.
newsitem.headline: Britain jails Palestinians for Israeli embassy bomb.

text.p: Two university-educated Palestinians were sentenced on Monday to 20 years in jail for their part in a 1994 bombing campaign against Jewish targets in London.
Jawad Botmeh, 28, and his female partner Samar Alami, 30, were convicted last week of conspiracy to cause explosions involving the Israeli embassy in London and a Jewish charity.
No-one was killed or seriously injured in the blasts.

Alami, from a wealthy and respected family and Botmeh, also a middle-class Palestinian, both obtained science degrees at British universities which the prosecution at the trial alleged gave them the knowledge they needed to make explosives.
"It comes as no surprise to me that your families were profoundly shocked," said Judge Patrick Garland, announcing their sentence.

"It has happened before and it will happen again, that blameless hard-working, well-regarded graduates from families held in high regard have a dark side, utterly unsuspected by those close to them until an explosion or the discovery of a terrorist arsenal," Garland added.
The judge recommended both should be deported at the end of their sentences.
Alami and Botneh had both pleaded not guilty to the charges.
The judge last week released a third man, Mahmoud Abu-Wardeh, clearing him of all charges at the end of a two-month trial.
In November another Palestinian woman, 49-year-old Nadia Zekra, was freed when the judge said there was not enough evidence against her.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants believed Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to be misguided in his attempts to seek peace with Israel and they carried out the bombings in the hope of damaging the Middle East peace process.

The Israeli embassy and Balfour House, a Jewish charity in north London, were blasted after Israeli leader Yitzhak Rabin and King Hussein of Jordan had signed the Washington Declaration which "paved the way for peace between their two countries".
Police traced the pair after finding a cache of arms and bomb ingredients in a safe deposit box. Evidence linked Botmeh and Alami to it.
